questions.question: What is the central invariant for choosing between the two model families?
options: Choose the narrowest learning objective that can produce the required output under real constraints
Always use the model with the most parameters
Use a generative model whenever labels exist
Use a discriminative model whenever inputs are numeric
questions.explanation: The product output, available evidence, assumptions, latency, safety, and operational budget determine whether learning a richer distribution creates useful value.

questions.question: Which quantity does a discriminative probabilistic classifier model directly?
questions.explanation: A discriminative classifier directly estimates the target conditional on the observed input or learns an equivalent decision score.

questions.question: Which requirement most clearly needs a generative objective?
questions.explanation: Creating new observations requires a model that represents enough of the data distribution to sample plausible outputs.

questions.question: In the worked three-class, 20-feature example, why does Gaussian Naive Bayes have 123 modeled values?
options: Each class has 20 means, 20 variances, and one prior
questions.explanation: For each of three classes, the example estimates 20 means, 20 variances, and one class prior: 3 x 41 = 123.

questions.question: How can Gaussian Naive Bayes handle a feature that is not observed at inference time?
options: Omit that feature's likelihood term and renormalize using observed evidence and class priors
Assume the missing value proves the positive class
questions.explanation: Under the model assumptions, marginalizing an absent feature removes its likelihood contribution. Less evidence should usually reduce confidence.

questions.question: Why is mean imputation part of a discriminative model's production contract?
options: The fill value changes the input presented to the learned decision boundary
It makes missingness impossible in production
It converts every classifier into a generative model
questions.explanation: A different fill value can change the direct score or cross the decision threshold, so preprocessing and missingness rules must be versioned with the model.

questions.question: What is a major failure risk of the Gaussian Naive Bayes formulation?
options: Correlated features can violate its conditional-independence assumption and distort confidence
It can never return a class prediction
It requires a GPU for every feature
questions.explanation: The simple factorization is efficient, but wrong distributional and independence assumptions can yield miscalibrated likelihoods and posteriors.

questions.question: Which production evaluation is appropriate for both model families?
options: Representative quality, calibration where relevant, latency, cost, drift, safety, and failure slices
questions.explanation: A production decision needs end-to-end evidence for the artifact users consume and the operating constraints the system must satisfy.
